result:
No Revisit dates have passed. The next one is 2 December, for the bake-to-order decision.

I didn't include a free first box or 50% off the first month. You dropped both on 6 Oct 2026: of 52 people who got a free box, only 6 started paying, and the free boxes took Saturday slots that paying customers wanted. The free box comes back only if paid signups fall below 8 a month for 2 months in a row. October had 15, so that condition isn't met. The 50% off can come back only if it's tested through a referral from an existing subscriber, and that's my first idea.

**1. Referrals from your 140 subscribers.** Give each subscriber a code to pass on: the friend gets 50% off their first month and the subscriber gets a free loaf or pastry. This is exactly the test your ledger allows. The difference from September is that a current customer vouches for you, instead of the offer going to anyone who wants free bread. Limit it to a set number of codes each week so it can't fill your Saturday slots. Track how many of these people keep paying after month one and compare that with the 6 in 52.

**2. Flyers on your own delivery routes.** Your bikes already pass the neighbours of 140 paying households every Saturday. Drop a small card in nearby letterboxes, for example "Your neighbour at no. 12 gets Sunday Crust bread on Saturdays", with a QR code that goes straight to signup. Printing costs roughly €50–80, well within your €300 budget, and it reaches people who are definitely inside your 3 km.

**3. A full-price, one-off box, collected at the shop.** Some people won't sign up because they don't want a subscription, not because of the price. Sell a single box at €18 for collection on Friday evening or Saturday. It isn't free or discounted, so it doesn't reopen what you dropped, and collection means it doesn't use a delivery slot. Put a "start weekly delivery" card in every box.

If you go ahead with any of these, I'll log it in the ledger. If you run the referral test, I'll also note it in the no-free-trial record, since it tests one of that record's reopen conditions.
